newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Busang gold plot thickens, seen hurting Indonesia.
newsitem.headline: Busang gold plot thickens, seen hurting Indonesia.

text.p: A senior Indonesian mining official said on Thursday the latest twist in the Busang gold discovery saga could dent the country's image and possibly investor confidence.
"I am sad," Kuntoro Mangkusubroto, director-general at the ministry of mines and energy, told reporters.
"What has happened will have an impact on the image of the country...and investments," he said. "Although it is just one case, it took place in Indonesia."

His comments followed an admission by Canadian exploration company Bre-X Minerals Ltd that gold resources in the Busang property could be far less than its previous estimate of some 71 million ounces worth around $25 billion.

The small, Calgary-based company had become the darling of the Toronto Stock Exchange due to ever-mounting reports last year on the amount of gold in the property in Indonesia's East Kalimantan, billed as the biggest single find since gold was discovered on South Africa's Witwatersrand late last century.

But the bubble burst on Wednesay when Bre-X chief executive David Walsh said in a statement from Calgary: "There appears to be a strong possibility that the potential gold resources...have been overstated".

Bre-X shares, suspended on Wednesday, were hit last week by news that its chief geologist, Michael de Guzman, had fallen out of a helicopter on his way to Busang. Some officials said he may have committed suicide.
Kuntoro said although Indonesia had not suffered any material loss, unlike Bre-X shareholders, the country's name would be affected.
He also said applications for contracts of work by Bre-X to further explore and develop the Busang property would be kept aside until the company submits a report.
"We have written to the company asking for a report," he said, adding that no deadline was given to Bre-X.

The contracts of work have been pending approval since last year when a bidding war for the Busang property took shape among Canada's Barrick Gold Corp, Placer Dome and Teck Corp Indonesian tin miner PT Tambang Timah also showed an interest.

But Indonesian tycoon and close associate of President Suharto, Muhammad "Bob" Hasan, entered the scene and picked U.S. mining giant Freeport McMoran Copper and Gold Inc as partner and operator of the propsed Busang gold mine.
A spokeswoman for Hasan's company said on Thursday the deal was subject to the property's economic feasibility.
Official sources said the government might review laws governing the booming mining sector with a view to ensuring there were no repeat of incidents such as the Busang case.
"Laws might have to be tightened," one official said. "But we are waiting for more information before doing anything."

M. Simatupang, vice-chairman of the Indonesian Mining Association, said that with the possible downgrading of the size of the Busang gold deposit, the project's contribution to the Indonesian economy would also be diminished.

"Previously, it was thought to be a significant contributor in terms of opening up East Kalimantan, corporate taxes and employment," he said. "But if what has been said is true, its contribution would be smaller."
"Mining has its risks. Not all companies are successful," he said, adding that the Busang picture would get clearer over the next few days as more details emerge.
